title: Stage 4 representative selection - the lawful rule that reduces two Gate 3 admitted candidates to one validation representative

serialisation.decimal_representation: Every fraction is a JSON string, parsed as an exact Decimal.

why_a_selection_is_needed.gate_3_outcome: Gate 3 Attempt 2 admitted TWO candidates and ranked neither. reports/stage3_attempt2/STAGE_3_ATTEMPT_2_DEVELOPMENT_ADMISSIBILITY.json records selection_made false and ranking_computed false; the Gate 3 Attempt 2 research report states on the record that Gate 3 admitted both and ranked neither.
why_a_selection_is_needed.why_both_cannot_go_forward: The validation window may be read once. Running both candidates on it would make the reported result a maximum over two draws, and the candidate carried to the holdout would then have been chosen on a validation outcome. That is selection on the out-of-sample window, which is the failure mode the three-partition design exists to prevent.
why_a_selection_is_needed.why_a_combination_is_not_the_answer: Combining, averaging, or forming a portfolio of C1 and C2 creates a third strategy that no gate has evaluated. Under constitution section 11 it is a new candidate and restarts at Gate 3. It is also not authorized by the operating instruction for this stage.
why_a_selection_is_needed.conclusion: Exactly one of the two admitted candidates must be selected, by a rule that is prospectively defensible and that does not read a validation observation.

search_for_a_mandatory_constitutional_se.question: Does the constitution, or any frozen or sealed artifact, already mandate how to reduce multiple admitted candidates to one?
searched: reports/stage3_attempt2/*, both evidence files and the design and research reports
search_for_a_mandatory_constitutional_se.result: No mandatory selection rule exists. The constitution's section 9 defines gate conjunction within a candidate and says nothing about choosing among candidates that pass. No sealed artifact carries a ranking rule, a tie-break, or a primary-candidate designation.
search_for_a_mandatory_constitutional_se.consequence: A rule must be constructed for this stage. Constitution section 8 permits it - it requires a signed specification created before execution - but the rule must be constructed from frozen and sealed material, must be prospectively defensible, and must not be a rationalisation of a preferred outcome.

constraint_that_did_apply.effect: The eligible set is exactly the two admitted PRIMARY candidates. No robustness neighbour of either is eligible, however it performed.

selection_rule.name: Declared-variant research-shutdown screen
selection_rule.statement: Eliminate any Gate 3 admitted candidate for which ANY of its declared runs - the PRIMARY parameterisation, any of its four declared robustness neighbours, or its section 7 required stressed-cost run - tripped the section 5.1 research shutdown on development data. If exactly one candidate survives, it is the representative. If both survive or neither survives, the rule does not decide and the stage stops for human selection.
selection_rule.applied_to: Development-window evidence only, already authorized and already read.
selection_rule.output_is_binary_per_variant: Each declared run either tripped the shutdown or did not. The rule counts trips. It does not compare magnitudes, does not rank, and has no threshold of its own to choose.

provenance.principle: Every term of the rule is taken from a frozen or sealed artifact. Nothing in it is a number this stage picked.

terms.term: the set of declared runs over which the screen operates
terms.note: The one PRIMARY plus four robustness neighbours per candidate were declared before any Attempt 2 strategy code was written, and the stressed-cost run was required by constitution section 7. The screen therefore operates over a variant set that was fixed before any of the runs existed. It is not a set this stage assembled.

That sealed field states the shutdown was enforced for the primaries, for all four neighbours of each candidate individually, and for the three non-gating stressed runs, and was disabled only for the labelled SPY buy-and-hold reference account. The screen's scope is the scope the shutdown was already enforced at. It is not a scope this stage widened.

why_it_is_prospectively_defensible: It is return-blind. The predicate never reads a total return, a Sharpe ratio, a profit factor, a drawdown magnitude, a trade count, or a benchmark comparison. It reads one boolean per declared run: did the sealed risk rule fire.
It has no free parameter. There is no threshold to tune, no weighting to choose, no window over which to measure, and no tie-break to invent. Every quantity comes from a frozen or sealed artifact.

It selects on a governance property rather than on performance. A candidate whose declared variant set contains a run that breached the project's own permanent risk rule is a candidate whose parameterisation sits on the boundary of what the project's risk architecture tolerates. Carrying that to a single-read out-of-sample window is the choice with the higher chance of producing an uninterpretable result, because a shutdown mid-validation truncates the window and forecloses the fold condition.

It is forward-looking in its justification. It answers 'which candidate can be evaluated on a once-readable window with the better chance of the evaluation being interpretable', not 'which candidate did better'.

It would have eliminated the same candidate under reversed returns. The predicate is a function of shutdown events only, so if C1's returns had exceeded C2's at every variant, C1 would still be eliminated and C2 would still be selected. This is the property that distinguishes a prospective rule from a retrospective one, and it is checkable by reading the predicate rather than by trusting the author.
It is stricter than a performance rule would be. A performance rule would have admitted C1 had its return been higher. This rule does not, because a shutdown is not offset by a return.
what_the_rule_is_not: It is not a ranking. It produces a survivor set, not an order. Had both candidates survived it would have decided nothing, and the stage would have stopped for human selection rather than reaching for a second criterion.
It is not a claim that C1 is a bad strategy. C1 satisfied every hard Gate 3 condition and remains a Gate 3 admitted candidate on the record. It is not carried to validation.
It is not a repair of C1. Repairing C1's cost sensitivity or its neighbour breach would be a parameter change creating a new candidate under section 11, and is explicitly not authorized.
It is not a rule about magnitudes. C1's breaching drawdowns and C2's largest non-breaching drawdown are recorded below for completeness, but the predicate uses neither.
selection_rule.honest_limitation: The rule was authored in a session in which Gate 3 development evidence was lawfully visible. Return-blindness makes the rule's OUTPUT independent of the returns; it does not make the CHOICE of predicate independent of the researcher's knowledge of the evidence. A different return-blind predicate - say, one screening on neighbour dispersion - might have selected differently. That residual freedom is disclosed here and in config/stage4_validation_protocol.json adaptive_research_disclosure rather than argued away. What limits it is that the predicate has no tunable part: once 'shutdown trip over the declared variant set' is chosen, the answer is fixed by the evidence and cannot be nudged.

evidence_source.fields_read: results.all_registered_variants[label].shutdown_session and .max_drawdown, and results.stressed_cost_runs[candidate].stressed_shutdown_session and .stressed_max_drawdown. Development window only.

corroborated_by.note: Section 20 items 2 and 3 of that report state both C1 shutdown events on the record independently of the JSON evidence file.

outcome.if_the_rule_had_not_decided: The stage would have stopped with a BLOCKED verdict and referred the selection to a human, rather than reaching for a second criterion. A tie-break invented after the first rule failed would be a retrospective rule wearing a prospective rule's clothes.

honest_qualification_of_the_margin.statement: C2 survives the screen without a single trip, but not with wide margins on every variant. Its largest non-breaching development drawdown is SE100-S3A2-C2-MEANREV-RA1#N2 at 0.1465979382684879116079616515992935, which is 34 basis points below the 15% shutdown level, and #N1 at 0.1438752249862801387348381472146044 is 61 basis points below it.
honest_qualification_of_the_margin.why_it_is_recorded: The screen is binary and those variants did not trip, so the rule's output is unaffected. But a reader entitled to know how close the surviving candidate came should not have to derive it. C2 is the survivor of this screen; it is not a candidate with comfortable risk headroom.
honest_qualification_of_the_margin.consequence_for_gate_4: S4-C3's ceiling is the same 15% on the same series (S4-CONFLICT-3). A representative whose development neighbours sat 34 basis points from that level has no margin to spare on a fresh window, and the drawdown condition is a real risk of failure, not a formality. This is recorded before any validation observation exists.

corroboration_not_used_in_the_decision.purpose: The screen decided on shutdown trips alone. These figures are recorded to show that the rule was not reverse-engineered from a preferred answer: every rule constructible from a FROZEN threshold points the same way, and none points at C1. If the screen had been built to reach a chosen answer, there would be no reason for the independent checks to agree with it.
corroboration_not_used_in_the_decision.status: NOT_DECISIVE. None of these comparisons is part of selection_rule.statement, and none was needed to reach the outcome.

checks.check: Development profit factor against Gate 4's FROZEN threshold of 1.15
checks.note: Gate 3's floor was 1.10, which C1 cleared. Gate 4 raises it to 1.15, which C1's development figure does not reach. This is a development figure and is not a prediction of C1's validation profit factor.

checks.check: Development Sharpe at the sealed 0% cash rate against Gate 4's FROZEN threshold of 0.50
checks.note: NEITHER candidate reaches 0.50 on development data. The comparison favours C2 but does not favour a Gate 4 pass for either, and that is recorded as an expectation in config/stage4_validation_protocol.json adaptive_research_disclosure.

checks.check: Stressed-cost development total return against Gate 4's FROZEN requirement that it remain positive
checks.c1: 0.0018, positive by 18 basis points, with the shutdown having fired on 2018-02-05
checks.note: C1's stressed run technically remained positive. It did so while breaching the risk rule, which is why the screen eliminates on the trip rather than on the return.

checks.check: Development maximum drawdown headroom against Gate 4's FROZEN ceiling of 15%

corroboration_not_used_in_the_decision.agreement_statement: Every check agrees with the screen. None was consulted to build it, and none would change its output. The one check that does NOT flatter the selected candidate - the Sharpe comparison, where C2's 0.42 is itself below Gate 4's floor - is recorded in the same list rather than omitted.

prohibited_after_this_seal: Changing the representative for any reason, including a Gate 4 FAIL.
Substituting SE100-S3A2-C1-PULLBACK-RA1 after a C2 validation result exists, or running it on validation as a comparison.
Substituting any robustness neighbour of C2. SE100-CFG-3004 neighbour_status: 'No. Never. Under no result.'
Changing any parameter of the sealed parameterisation.
Adding a risk overlay, a position-size cap, a regime filter, or any other rule not in the sealed specification.
Reinterpreting the selection rule, or applying a different return-blind rule, after a validation result exists.

adaptation_disclosure.statement: This selection was made in a session that had lawful access to Gate 3 development evidence. It is an adaptive step, not an independent one.
adaptation_disclosure.what_is_independent: The rule's output. Given the predicate, the answer is a function of shutdown booleans recorded in a sealed evidence file, and no return enters it.
adaptation_disclosure.what_is_not_independent: The choice of predicate. It was chosen by a researcher who had read the development evidence, and a different return-blind predicate could in principle have selected differently.
how_it_is_mitigated: The predicate has no tunable parameter, so it cannot be nudged toward an outcome once chosen.
The full application is recorded for BOTH candidates, including every variant that did not trip, so a reader can verify the count rather than trust it.
The independent frozen-threshold checks are recorded, including the one that does not flatter the selected candidate.
The surviving candidate's narrowest margin is recorded rather than left to be discovered.
The rule's return-blindness is stated as a checkable property of the predicate, not as an assurance about the author's state of mind.
adaptation_disclosure.not_concealed: The representative keeps its Gate 3 identifier unchanged, so it is traceable to the evidence that admitted it and to the two-attempt search that produced it.
